Whoever embraces Islam sincerely or follows it well has good deeds rewarded ten to seven hundred times, while an evil deed is recorded only as it is.
Three men shut in a cave by a rock each invoke Allah by a deed done for His sake, and the rock moves away bit by bit.
Hakim bin Hizam asks about the kin ties he kept, slaves he freed and alms he gave before Islam, and the Prophet says he embraced Islam with those good deeds.
Three men trapped in a cave by a rock invoke Allah by deeds done for His sake: serving parents, leaving a cousin untouched and paying a labourer's grown wages.
Three men shut in a cave by a rock invoke Allah by deeds done for His sake, and Allah removes the rock.
Allah thanked and forgave a man who removed a thorny branch from the road.
Hakim bin Hizam freed slaves and slaughtered camels before and after Islam, and the Prophet told him he had embraced Islam with all the good deeds he had done.
An older companion serves Anas, having vowed to serve any Ansari; Anas serves the Prophet; those not fasting serve and take the reward; helping a rider is charity.
A slave who falls ill or travels is rewarded like the good deeds he did at home in health, as Abu Burda tells Yazid, who fasted on journeys.
A man who kissed a woman told the Prophet, and the verse came that prayer and good deeds remove evil deeds, which the Prophet said is for all his followers.
A horse brings reward, protection or sin according to why it is kept; for donkeys the Prophet cites the verse that every atom's weight of good or evil is seen.
The deeds most loved are regular ones even if few; act moderately within your ability, for deeds alone admit none to Paradise, not even the Prophet, without Allah's mercy.
Allah declares war on whoever is hostile to His pious worshipper, who draws near through obligations, then extra deeds, until loved, and Allah becomes his hearing, sight, hand and leg.
Allah will shade seven on Resurrection Day, including one refusing a noble woman's call to illegal intercourse; the Prophet guarantees Paradise to whoever guards his tongue and private parts.
A bad deed only intended is not written, and abandoned for Allah's sake it counts as good; a good deed intended counts as one, and done, ten to seven hundred.
